planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Zijuan is a tropical, broad-leaved Yunnan selection best suited to USDA zones 8-10.

directions: Zijuan is a distinctive Yunnan large-leaf tea cultivar selected for its naturally deep purple leaves, buds, and stems, a trait caused by unusually high anthocyanin pigment levels rather than any processing step. It was bred from broad-leaved assamica-type tea stock native to Yunnan's mountains, and is processed into both loose green tea and purple-tinted pressed cakes, with the leaf retaining a purplish cast even after drying and a brew that takes on a pale lavender-to-pink hue depending on water chemistry and steep time. Grow it like other large-leaf Yunnan tea plants, in warm, humid conditions with acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil and regular moisture, and expect a more tender, slower-hardening plant than the small-leaved Japanese and Chinese China-type cultivars. Its high anthocyanin and polyphenol content has also made it popular for specialty 'purple tea' marketing emphasizing antioxidant content.

common_name: Hong Yu Tea (Ruby 18, Taiwan Tea No. 18)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Hong Yu is a vigorous, broad-leaved cultivar best suited to USDA zones 8-10.

directions: Hong Yu, officially registered by Taiwan's Tea Research and Extension Station as Taiwan Tea No. 18 and widely marketed as 'Ruby 18' or 'Red Jade,' was bred from a cross between wild Taiwanese mountain tea and a large-leaf Burmese assamica-type parent. It is best known as the signature cultivar behind Sun Moon Lake black tea, prized for a naturally sweet, honeyed black-tea liquor with a distinctive mint-and-cinnamon aroma that requires no flavoring additives. The plant is a vigorous, broad-leaved, assamica-influenced shrub that performs best in warm, humid conditions with acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil, and it is markedly less cold-hardy than small-leaved China-type cultivars. Regular plucking of the top two leaves and a bud keeps the bush productive and encourages the tender new growth prized for black tea manufacture.
sources: Taiwan Tea Research and Extension Station

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings in spring in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade to full sun; Tukdah Tea is best suited to USDA zones 8-10.

directions: Tukdah is one of the older clonal selections developed for the Darjeeling tea gardens of West Bengal, India, and remains a widely planted reference clone across the region's high-elevation estates. It is a China-type, small-leaved selection adapted to the cool, steep, mist-prone slopes of Darjeeling, producing a black tea valued for its brisk, floral character, though it is generally regarded as more workmanlike than the muscatel-forward specialty clones like AV2. Grow it in acidic, well-drained, humus-rich soil with partial shade and consistent moisture, expecting a slower-establishing, delicate plant typical of Darjeeling's China-type stock. As with other Darjeeling selections, careful withering and oxidation during processing are key to developing its characteristic cup quality.
sources: Tea Research Association, Tocklai Tea Research Institute, India
